Amelia / Michael — I reviewed the MSA and sketched an initial set of comments. High-level notes up front (I’ll upload a tracked PDF early Tuesday):

1) Data handling / residency: Redwood’s baseline MSA describes hosted processing in the US with standard SOC2 controls; customers that require EU residency or dedicated tenancy sign an Exhibit B. Please confirm whether Novaforge will require EU residency for any subset of data — if yes, flag which product lines and which environments.

2) Indemnity & IP: There are a couple of customer-side redlines we commonly see (narrower indemnity, clarification of infringement notice). I have proposed modest language to preserve our warranty and liability caps while addressing common procurement concerns.

3) Order Form: I noticed Novaforge provided a signatory matrix but no billing cadence. Laura, can you confirm monthly vs. annual billing and whether Novaforge needs a PO number on invoices?

4) SLA / uptime: Redwood provides SLA language for Dedicated contracts; for Hosted customers we include an operational SLO table but no formal SLA unless in a Dedicated commitment. Amelia — please confirm whether Novaforge expects SLA-backed credits in the initial contract.

Proposed plan: I’ll send a version with inline tracked changes and a short summary (three bullets per section) tomorrow morning. If Novaforge wants us to accept a counter-orderform edit, please track the specific clauses you’d like amended (pricing, seat counts, residency).

Thanks — quick replies to the 3 clarifying points above would help speed assumptions.

-Kim

Hi Kim / Michael,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from the Novaforge side:

- Residency: We do not need EU residency at the MSA level right now — product teams may request EU-only storage for a subset later; we’ll raise that as an amendment if/when it’s required.
- Billing cadence: Novaforge prefers annual invoicing with net-30 payment terms. PO requirement: yes, we will issue a PO; please include a PO field on the invoice.
- SLA expectations: We’d like the hosted SLA credits to be considered for the pilot phase, but it’s not a hard blocker — please propose your standard hosted SLO table and we’ll raise any exceptions.

We’ll review Kimberly’s tracked changes once received. If you can also confirm the Redwood signatory (name and title) for the MSA, we can map signers on our side.
